def:
Identify Controller field giving, as a 0's based count of logical blocks, the largest write the controller guarantees to be atomic with respect to other commands during normal operation. Its companion AWUPF covers power failure; namespace-level NAWUN/NAWUPF and atomic boundary fields can override or constrain it.
Common confusion: assuming a 4 KiB write is atomic without reading these fields.

Bit 29 of CDW12 in NVM I/O commands. When set, the controller inserts protection information on writes and strips it on reads, so the host neither supplies nor receives it (for an 8-byte metadata format). When clear, the host supplies and receives the PI tuple and the controller passes it through, checking the fields selected by PRCHK.
Common confusion: PRACT = 1 does not disable protection; it moves generation to the controller.

Bits 28:26 of CDW12 in NVM I/O commands selecting which protection information fields the controller checks: guard (bit 28), application tag (bit 27) and reference tag (bit 26). Fields not selected are not checked for that command, even on a namespace formatted with PI.

term: Optimal I/O hints (NPWG, NPWA, NPDG, NPDA, NOWS)
exp: Namespace Preferred Write Granularity / Alignment, Preferred Deallocate Granularity / Alignment, Optimal Write Size
def: Identify Namespace fields that tell the host the write and deallocate sizes and alignments the device handles most efficiently. They are performance hints: ignoring them is legal but may cause internal read-modify-write. Linux maps them to the block device's minimum and optimal I/O sizes.
